title: Native run summary
description: NT-04c: the small committed summary of one classified native run (scripts/native-acceptance/runs/<opf version>/<target>.json): per file the score and class of every slide as it stood after review. The next release's run is classified against it. scripts/native-acceptance/core/classify/README.md explains it.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this format. Always 1.

tier.description: The run's tier; null for a run that was not a tier run. candidate: the smoke tier plus the release-tier files whose slides changed since the baseline (NT-13).

note.description: How the summary was made, when not by `pnpm native` (for example a one-time import of a round's hand grades).

settings.description: The classifier's threshold and tolerance the classes were given with.

warnings.description: The distinct import-warning lines of the run, the application's wording, with how many files showed each.

scores.description: One picture score per slide, rounded to 5 places; null where the slide was not compared.

classes.description: One letter per slide: s same, k known-present, g known-gone, n new, - not-compared.

known.description: The record ids per slide number, for the slides that have any.

import.description: Whether OPF imported the application's copy (verbs.resave.import).

importError.description: The importer's error code when the import failed (invalid-chart-cache ...).

outcomes.description: Object outcomes counted by "<kind>.<outcome>". Summed per kind they are the exported objects of that kind, which the classifier compares before it compares outcomes.

export.description: NT-13: what the exported file draws, as hashes (scripts/native-acceptance/core/select/slide-parts.mjs, the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256). deck covers the parts every slide shares (masters, the layouts slides use, theme, presentation properties); slides has one hash per slide, over the slide part and every part it reaches (charts, diagrams, pictures, media, notes, tags). A release candidate opens only the files whose hashes differ.
